summary: During the planned monster-turn simulation, a future monster death creates a green-slime glob and reaches obj_nexto_xy. The corpse helper already receives the planning random provider, but obj_nexto discards it; obj_nexto_xy then uses the live core RNG for its two ordering draws. Those speculative draws advance the real stream before the current monster's resist_conflict roll, producing the v83 step-662 mismatch. Pass the caller's random provider through the glob-search helper and its recursive calls.

source.branch: The recursive search runs when a corpse is a glob and no matching glob is already under the death square. Its two rn2(2) calls must use the random stream supplied by the active caller; during planned turns that stream is cloned, while live calls retain the core stream.
callers: mon.c:make_corpse creates a glob and calls obj_nexto to merge nearby globs; the JavaScript caller already has the planned random provider in make_corpse's object environment.
do.c:flooreffects searches nearby globs through obj_nexto_xy; its JavaScript caller carries rawEnv.random when invoked in a planned action.

evidence: The accepted v83 comparison at step 662 has 3425 JavaScript versus 3424 C RNG calls. At RNG index 2951 C next records rnd(20)=10 at mondata.c:resist_conflict, while JavaScript records rn2(2)=1; screen and cursor also diverge at the same action boundary.

Prep's saved stack trace in .cache/prep47-recovery/prep83/logs/slime-nexto-trace.log shows obj_nexto_xy -> obj_nexto -> make_corpse -> mondied -> monkilled during the speculative monster attack, with state !== game. The paired provenance is in slime-nexto-provenance.json.

C mkobj.c:obj_nexto_xy (3661-3693) makes exactly two global rn2(2) draws only when recurs is true, and propagates the same random walk into recurs=false calls. mon.c:make_corpse (706-729) uses this search only while merging a newly created slime/pudding glob; do.c:flooreffects (308-315) is the other production caller.

JavaScript mon.js:make_corpse constructs objectEnv.random from the caller's injected provider, but calls obj_nexto(obj,state) without passing it. js/obj.js:obj_nexto_xy uses imported coreRn2 directly and discards any caller-specific stream. The planning simulator already runs monster actions with clonedRandom(planned), so threading that provider through these two helpers prevents speculative RNG from advancing the live stream.
